analysis.title: Everyone Is Dumping Gold. Here's The Problem.
key_insights: Gold is testing critical levels after a sharp washout. ETF outflows are accelerating and CTAs are running sizable shorts, which sets up a potential positioning squeeze.

The $4,000 level is the key support for gold and held several times this summer. Gold trades well below its 200-day moving average, with initial resistance near $4,125 where the 21-day moving average sits.
GLD recorded its biggest weekly outflow since March, so investors are selling after the washout and may be selling into the lows.
CTAs are running sizable gold shorts. The last time positioning was this bearish came just before the August short squeeze.
Goldman's CTA models suggest momentum-driven buying if gold starts recovering. Heavily short systematic positioning could force CTAs to cover and then flip to buyers.
The dollar is the main obstacle. Gold and the dollar have moved in an almost perfect inverse relationship this year, and a sustained gold rebound may need the dollar to roll over first.
risk_factors: The dollar may keep strengthening and cap any gold rebound, given the near-perfect inverse relationship this year.
A break below $4,000 support would remove the level that held several times this summer.
